findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra storage lookup
findings.body: In remove(), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked inside the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; when the cache entry was valid, the code relied solely on the already-cached `CachedIdentityProvider` without hitting the underlying storage. With this change, every call to remove() now performs an unconditional read against the delegate storage provider (JPA), even when a valid cached copy is already available, just to determine whether to invalidate the login caches. This is a measurable regression on a hot path (IDP removal) and could have been avoided by reusing the already-fetched `cached.getIdentityProvider()` when present.

findings.title: Login cache invalidation is always applied to all three fetch modes, causing cache thrashing for multi-organization realms
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation() and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() always invalidate the cache keys for all three FetchMode values (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) whenever any IDP crosses login-eligibility, regardless of which organization (if any) is actually affected. Unlike getByOrganization(), which caches/invalidates per specific organization id (cacheKeyOrgId), the getForLogin() cache stores results for ALL organizations' queries inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery keyed only by realm+mode. This means a single IDP update unrelated to a particular organization wipes out cached login results for every organization in the realm, causing unnecessary cache misses and re-queries in realms with many organizations.

findings.title: Single cache entry per mode can accumulate unbounded per-organization result sets
findings.body: getForLogin() caches results under a single key per FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin), with per-organization result sets stored inside the same IdentityProviderListQuery object (keyed internally by organizationId as the search key). In realms with many organizations, repeated getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, orgId) calls for different organizations will keep adding entries to the same cached object indefinitely, since there is no per-org eviction — only a full invalidation of the whole mode-level entry. This can lead to unbounded growth of a single cache entry in multi-tenant/many-organization deployments.

findings.title: Asymmetric isEnabled() evaluation between original and updated model in login invalidation check
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated) is called from update() with `original` being the result of getById(), which wraps the model through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (its isEnabled() depends dynamically on the linked organization's current enabled state). The `updated` parameter, however, is the raw model passed into update() and uses the static isEnabled() field value. When the organization is currently disabled, getLoginPredicate().test(original) and getLoginPredicate().test(updated) can diverge purely due to this wrapping difference rather than due to an actual change in the IDP, leading to unnecessary cache invalidations. While this does not appear to cause stale caches (it only triggers extra invalidation), the asymmetry is inconsistent and could mask more serious issues if the wrapping logic changes in the future.

findings.title: Public static predicate semantics changed without versioning/compat note
findings.body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() is a public static method on a server-spi interface, and its behavior has been changed to additionally require that organization-linked IDPs have BROKER_PUBLIC=true. Any existing external code (custom providers, extensions) that already calls this public API expecting the old semantics (only ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN checks) will now silently get different results. Since server-spi is a public extension point, this behavior change should be called out explicitly (e.g., in release notes or javadoc) as it is a backward-incompatible semantic change to a public method, not just an internal implementation detail.

findings.title: No test coverage for the isEnabled() re-check fix introduced in the login IDP bean
findings.body: This PR adds `idp.isEnabled()` re-checks in searchForIdentityProviders() for the ORG_ONLY and ALL branches, specifically to handle the case where a cached IDP model is wrapped and its effective isEnabled() depends on live organization enablement status that may differ from what was cached. No test was added (in OrganizationCacheTest or elsewhere) that exercises this specific scenario, e.g. disabling an organization after the login IDP list has been cached and verifying that disabled-org IDPs are filtered out of the rendered login page bean. Without such a test, a regression in this filtering logic (e.g. someone removing the re-check) would not be caught.
